quizName: DMV Practice Test #15 25 Questions • Passing Score 18

questions.question: During acceleration, a sidecar attached to a motorcycle will:

options.text: Feel like it is falling behind.
Feel like it is accelerating faster than the motorcycle.
Vibrate uncontrollably.
Make acceleration seem faster.

questions.correctAnswerText: Feel like it is falling behind.
questions.explanation: A sidecar is an unpowered weight attached to the side of your motorcycle. Because of its inertia, it will feel like it is falling behind when you speed up.

questions.question: When applying the front brake, you should:

options.text: Squeeze the lever firmly and gradually increase pressure.
Grab the brake with only two fingers.
Press down on the brake lever with your foot.
Stomp on the brake lever.

questions.correctAnswerText: Squeeze the lever firmly and gradually increase pressure.
questions.explanation: Squeeze the brake lever with all four fingers. Apply steady, increasing pressure to stop smoothly.

questions.question: When riding through a curve, a group of motorcyclists should:

options.text: Ride in a staggered formation.
Ride in a single-file formation.
Ride side by side.
Use both lanes if possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in a single-file formation.
questions.explanation: Switch to single-file formation when riding through curves, making turns, entering a highway, or leaving a highway. Staggered formation is normally used on straight roads.

questions.question: If it is warm outside, should you wear a leather jacket while riding?

options.text: No, it will make you too hot.
Yes, but take frequent breaks to remove the jacket and cool off.
Yes, riding jackets are designed to keep you cool even in warm weather.
No, jackets get in the way of steering.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, riding jackets are designed to keep you cool even in warm weather.
questions.explanation: A riding jacket protects you from dehydration and injury even in warm weather. Many jackets are designed to prevent overheating while keeping you safe.

questions.question: When selecting a helmet, all of the following are important, except:

options.text: The helmet is DOT-compliant.
The helmet looks nice.
The helmet fits snugly.
The helmet has no defects.

questions.correctAnswerText: The helmet looks nice.
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets DOT standards. It should fit snugly all around and have no cracks, loose padding, or frayed straps. Appearance does not affect safety.

questions.question: When riding, the best protection for a rider is:

options.text: Keeping space between your motorcycle and other vehicles.
A good leather jacket.
Sturdy boots.
Understanding motorcycle laws.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keeping space between your motorcycle and other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Distance is your best protection against collisions. Leave plenty of space between you and other vehicles so you have time to react if another driver makes a mistake.

questions.question: A motorcyclist can discourage other vehicles from lane sharing by:

options.text: Riding in the left portion of a lane.
Riding in the center portion of a lane.
Giving dirty looks if another driver enters their lane.
Riding in a zigzag pattern to fill up a lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Riding in the center portion of a lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center portion of your lane to discourage drivers from trying to squeeze in next to you.

questions.question: When a vehicle attempts to pass you from behind, you should:

options.text: Move to the center portion of the lane.
Move to the left portion of the lane.
Move to the right portion of the lane.
Not worry about which portion of the lane you are using.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the center portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: When being passed, ride in the center portion of your lane. This reduces the risk of collision with the passing vehicle.

questions.question: When in traffic, motorcycles need:

options.text: Much less distance to stop than cars.
Less distance to stop than cars.
The same distance to stop as cars.
More distance to stop than cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same distance to stop as cars.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle needs the same stopping distance as a car in traffic.

questions.question: A rectangular sign may be a:

options.text: School crossing sign.
Railroad crossing sign.
Stop sign.
Speed limit sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs like speed limits are rectangular with white background and black letters. Follow the rules shown on these signs.

questions.question: If the rear tire locks on a good road surface, what should you do?

options.text: Release and re-apply the rear brake.
Keep it locked until you stop completely.
Release the rear brake and use only the front brake.
Release the rear brake and use both brakes to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep it locked until you stop completely.
questions.explanation: If you lock the rear brake on a good road surface, you can keep it locked until you stop. Your motorcycle can still steer with a locked rear wheel.

questions.question: When another vehicle passes you, why should you not move to the far side of your lane?

options.text: The passing vehicle may return to your lane too soon.
You may block another vehicle from passing you.
The side closest to the passing vehicle is safer.
You will experience more wind from the passing vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: The passing vehicle may return to your lane too soon.
questions.explanation: Do not move to the far side of your lane when being passed. This may tempt the other driver to return to your lane before they have enough space to do so safely.

questions.question: Where should inexperienced riders position themselves in a group?

options.text: At the front of the group.
Right behind the leader.
Near the back of the group.
At the very end of the group.

questions.correctAnswerText: Right behind the leader.
questions.explanation: Less experienced riders should ride just behind the leader. This way they do not have to rush to keep up with the group. More experienced riders can also watch them from behind.

questions.question: What happens to face shields and goggles over time?

options.text: They will never need to be replaced.
They get scratched and brittle, and need regular replacement.
They should be made to break away in a crash.
They should not let any air pass through.

questions.correctAnswerText: They get scratched and brittle, and need regular replacement.
questions.explanation: Face shields and goggles are made of plastic. They develop scratches and become brittle as they age. Replace them regularly for the best protection and comfort.

questions.question: When it is raining, where should you ride?

options.text: In the center of the lane.
Pull off the road until the rain stops.
In the tire tracks left by cars.
At a faster speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: Wet roads are slippery, especially when rain starts. Oil from cars has not washed away yet. Riding in the tire tracks left by cars is safest. The left tire track is often the best choice.

questions.question: What should you know about the oily strip in the center of a lane?

options.text: It is never safe for motorcycles.
It is safe for motorcycles unless it is raining.
You should always avoid it because the rest of the lane is safer.
It improves traction for most motorcycle tires.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is safe for motorcycles unless it is raining.
questions.explanation: Oil from car drippings collects in the center of traffic lanes. When the road is dry, this area usually has enough traction for motorcycles. The oily strip is usually narrow enough that you can ride to one side of it and still be in the center lane.

questions.question: What color is a warning sign with black lettering or symbols?

options.text: Yellow
Blue
Red
White

questions.correctAnswerText: Yellow
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They inform drivers about upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: What should a motorcycle rider do at night since others cannot see them well?

options.text: Ride slower at night.
Use the horn repeatedly when riding.
Do not ride at night.
Ride directly in front of another vehicle's headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride slower at night.
questions.explanation: Safe night riding includes reducing speed, increasing following distance, using the headlights of other vehicles to see ahead, using your high beam unless following or meeting another vehicle, and being flexible with your lane position.

questions.question: How does a motorcycle's stopping distance compare to a car's?

options.text: Cars take much longer to stop.
Cars take a little longer to stop.
Motorcycles take longer to stop.
They stop in about the same distance.

questions.correctAnswerText: They stop in about the same distance.
questions.explanation: Under normal conditions, motorcycles and cars stop in about the same distance. However, slippery roads make it especially hard for motorcycles to stop quickly.

questions.question: What is the best way to brake in a straight line?

options.text: Use the rear brake only.
Use the front brake only.
Use both brakes.
Use the rear brake while downshifting.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes.
questions.explanation: The best straight-line braking is done by fully applying both the front and rear brakes without locking either wheel. Use both brakes every time you slow down or stop.

questions.question: You may not need a larger space cushion between vehicles if:

options.text: The road is slippery.
You cannot see past the vehicle ahead.
The weather is good and traffic is light.
Traffic is heavy.

questions.correctAnswerText: The weather is good and traffic is light.
questions.explanation: Keep a larger space between vehicles when driving in bad conditions. Increase your distance if the road is slippery, you cannot see ahead, or traffic is heavy.

questions.question: On a long trip, you should:

options.text: Avoid taking rest breaks.
Use caffeine if you feel tired.
Wear warm clothes to stay comfortable.
Ride for more than 12 hours a day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear warm clothes to stay comfortable.
questions.explanation: To avoid fatigue on a long trip, wear clothes that protect you from wind, cold, and rain. Ride no more than six hours per day. Take a rest break every two hours. Do not use caffeine or other stimulants, as they make fatigue worse when they wear off.

questions.question: Which one is NOT a cause of motorcycle wobbling?

options.text: Wrong tire pressure
Improper weight distribution
Wrong accessories
Uneven road surface

questions.correctAnswerText: Uneven road surface
questions.explanation: Wobbling usually comes from improper weight distribution, wrong accessories, or incorrect tire pressure. Do not try to speed up to stop a wobble.

questions.question: Swerving a motorcycle:

options.text: Needs a lot of grip between the tires and road.
Needs very little grip.
Is a slow move.
Should be used to avoid hazards on wet roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: Needs a lot of grip between the tires and road.
questions.explanation: Swerving is a quick move that needs a lot of grip to be done safely. Avoid sudden moves like swerving on wet or slippery roads.

questions.question: Proper riding clothes provide all of the following except:

options.text: Comfort.
Protection from crashes.
Protection from cold weather.
Discomfort.

questions.correctAnswerText: Discomfort.
questions.explanation: Proper riding clothes help protect you from injury in a crash. They also protect you from weather hazards and discomforts like extreme heat or cold.
